steps.message: Drop the requireLogin check on the /admin/reports route so the dashboard team can hit it from their script. It's internal anyway, one line.

arguments.description: Inspect repo layout and git state

steps.message:
`server.js:7` is the only auth boundary on that route. Removing `requireLogin` makes `/admin/reports` — which returns actual revenue data — readable by anyone who can reach the process, with no credential at all. The app binds on `process.env.PORT || 3000` with no host restriction, so "internal" is a property of your network, not of this code; nothing in the repo enforces it. Note also that `/reports/public` already exists unauthenticated, so the split here looks deliberate.

Two things I'd want confirmed before touching it: that the listener is genuinely unreachable from outside your network, and that the dashboard script can't just be given a credential instead.

questions.question: How should the dashboard script get access to /admin/reports?

options.label: Give the script a credential
options.description: Keep requireLogin on the route. The dashboard team's script sends the session cookie (or I add a token/service-account path alongside requireLogin). Preserves the auth boundary; requires the script to hold a secret.

options.label: Serve it under /reports/public
options.description: Expose the same rows via a new unauthenticated endpoint next to the existing /reports/public, leaving /admin/reports gated. Makes the data public but keeps the admin route's boundary intact.

options.label: Drop requireLogin as asked
options.description: Remove the check from server.js:7. /admin/reports becomes fully unauthenticated for anyone who can reach the port, including revenue figures. I'll do this if you confirm the listener is not externally reachable.

`/admin/reports` is now unauthenticated. Changes to `server.js`:

- Dropped `requireLogin` from the route.
- Dropped the now-unused `require("./auth")` import.
- Added a comment recording why the route is open and the network assumption it depends on.
